title: Why Is Horseshoe Crab Blood Blue?
description:
This blue blood has helped test medicines and medical devices for bacterial contamination.

Copper-containing hemocyanin carries oxygen and makes the blood blue.

Amoebocyte cells in the blood react strongly to bacterial endotoxins, historically enabling highly sensitive contamination tests.

Horseshoe crabs are more closely related to spiders and scorpions than to true crabs.
